newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-HOLYFIELD TRAINING HARDER THAN EVER FOR TYSON REMATCH.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-HOLYFIELD TRAINING HARDER THAN EVER FOR TYSON REMATCH.

text.p: Evander Holyfield will be a better fighter in his rematch with Mike Tyson later this month than he was when he won their first bout, the heavyweight champion's trainer predicted Wednesday.
"He knows he has to be better, so he is training harder," said Holyfield trainer Don Turner in a telephone interview from the champion's Houston training camp.
"From what I've seen he is better than before, quicker, stronger, got more angles and is punching harder," Turner said.

"Evander knocked him out in 11 rounds in the first fight. If history is on our side, he should knock him out earlier this time," Turner said of the June 28 Las Vegas rematch in which both fighter's are expected to make about $30 million.
Holyfield's, whose stunning upset of Tyson last November 8 shocked the boxing world, has been in training since January for his World Boxing Association title defence.
The fight, originally scheduled for May 3, was pushed back after Tyson suffered a cut during sparring. But Holyfield never skipped a beat in his gruelling training regimen.
"He kept working, he kept up the strength programme," Turner said, adding that strength and conditioning coach Tim Hallmark never left Holyfield's side.
"At this point he is handling these guys much better than he did last time three, four weeks before the fight," Turner said, referring to Holyfield's sparring partners.
Holyfield (33-3) has trained with the idea that Tyson also will be sharper than the man he was thoroughly beating before the referee stopped the bout in the 11th round.

"He knows he is in for the fight of his life and every day in the gym he is not going to underestimate this man," Turner said of Tyson, who suffered only his second defeat in 47 professional bouts to Holyfield.
Tyson's handlers have said their fighter had not prepared well for the first fight, underestimating the 34-year-old Holyfield's ability after a series of unimpressive outings.
"When they come up with those excuses that only motivates him," Turner said of Holyfield.
"His goal is to prove to himself that he is one of the best heavyweights who every lived and June 28 he will prove it."
